title: Ukraine Support Act
official_title: To authorize support for Ukraine, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Passed the House narrowly, 226-195 (19 crossover votes), and was received in the Senate. Sponsored by Rep. Meeks (D-NY), the ranking member on Foreign Affairs, with 43 cosponsors. The close, largely partisan margin and the bill's mandatory sanctions triggers, 500% tariffs, and frozen-asset tax make clearing the 60-vote Senate threshold and earning a signature unlikely.
summary: Authorizes a broad package of U.S. support for Ukraine — diplomatic, economic, and military — and builds a Russia sanctions regime that the President must impose whenever he determines Russia is waging war on or refusing to negotiate peace with Ukraine, backed by tariffs, export controls, a tax on frozen Russian assets, and congressional review of any move to lift sanctions.
brief: Authorizes U.S. support for Ukraine and a Russia sanctions regime triggered whenever the President finds Russia is waging war or blocking peace.

top_lines.headline: Sanctions Triggered by a Russia War Determination
subs: Every 90 days the President must determine whether Russia is waging a war of aggression or refusing to negotiate peace
An affirmative finding forces sanctions on major Russian banks, oil/mining firms, top officials, Rosatom, and price-cap-violating vessels
Lifting any Russia sanction requires advance notice and a 30-day congressional review with a joint resolution of approval

top_lines.headline: Diplomatic and Reconstruction Support
subs: Creates a Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund funded by a new tax on income from frozen Russian sovereign assets
Authorizes $250M for Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty in FY2026 and $30M/year for U.S.-European nuclear cooperation
Condemns Russia's forced transfer of at least 19,000 Ukrainian children as an act of genocide

top_lines.headline: Military and Economic Pressure
subs: Extends Lend-Lease authority and the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative ($300M for FY2026 and FY2027) and raises the Ukraine/NATO direct-loan cap to $8B
Imposes a duty of at least 500% on Russian goods and a 100% tax on income from frozen Russian and Belarusian state assets
Bans imports of fuel refined from Russian crude and tightens dual-use export controls

items.main: Sets out findings on Russia's 2022 invasion and a sense of Congress backing Ukraine's sovereignty.
items.detail: Recounts Russia's February 24, 2022 full-scale invasion, documented war crimes, and the forced deportation of at least 19,000 Ukrainian children, and states that any peace must include Ukraine and its European allies, that Russian forces should withdraw including from Crimea and the Donbas, and that Putin and Russian leaders should be prosecuted for war crimes. This section is a non-binding statement of policy.

sections.label: Section 108 — Support for Radio Free Europe

items.main: Backs restoring Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty and authorizes funding for it.
items.detail: States that RFE/RL should be restored to full capacity, authorizes $250M for RFE/RL for fiscal year 2026, encourages opening new bureaus around Russia's periphery, and requires the President to report within 90 days on staffing and bureau recommendations.

items.main: Creates a Treasury trust fund for Ukraine's reconstruction, financed by the new tax on frozen Russian assets.
items.detail: Adds section 9512 to the Internal Revenue Code establishing the Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund, into which the net revenues from the section 316 tax on frozen Russian-asset income are deposited. The Secretary of State may use the funds, subject to appropriations, for reconstruction, humanitarian assistance, economic growth, and accountable governance in Ukraine, under Foreign Assistance Act requirements.

items.main: Directs a strategy to counter Russian influence in Europe's nuclear-energy sector and authorizes funding.
items.detail: Requires the Secretary of State, with the Secretary of Energy, to develop a strategy to strengthen U.S.-European nuclear cooperation and counter Russian malign influence (including an assessment of Rosatom), submitted within 120 days, and authorizes $30M for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029 to support that engagement.

items.main: Extends the Ukraine Lend-Lease authority and adds reporting on loaned defense articles.
items.detail: Amends the Ukraine Democracy Defense Lend-Lease Act of 2022 to extend the loan/lease authority from fiscal years 2022-2023 through fiscal years 2022 through 2028, and requires the Secretary of State to report within 90 days of any use of the authority on the articles provided and a plan for their recovery and return.

sections.label: Section 202 — Direct Loans and Foreign Military Financing

items.main: Raises the cap on direct loans to Ukraine and NATO allies to $8B.
items.detail: Authorizes direct loans under section 23 of the Arms Export Control Act for Ukraine and NATO allies through fiscal year 2026, with principal not to exceed $8B, and amends the Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2022 by raising its loan ceiling from $4B to $8B.

items.main: Authorizes military-capacity assistance for the Baltic states.
items.detail: Directs the Secretary of State to build the capacity of Baltic militaries and border forces under the 2024 Bilateral Defense Cooperation Roadmaps, and authorizes, for each of fiscal years 2026, 2027, and 2028, $30M in Foreign Military Financing and $4M in Nonproliferation, Anti-terrorism, Demining, and Related programs for each Baltic country.

sections.label: Section 204 — Extension of Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative

items.main: Extends and funds the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative through 2027.
items.detail: Amends section 1250 of the FY2016 NDAA to authorize $300M for the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative for each of fiscal years 2026 and 2027 and extends the program's authority from December 31, 2026 to December 31, 2027.

items.main: Sets up the recurring determination that activates the bill's mandatory sanctions.
items.detail: Requires the President, within 15 days of enactment and at least every 90 days thereafter, to determine whether Russia or a proxy is conducting a war of aggression against Ukraine, refusing to sincerely negotiate peace, or violating a negotiated peace agreement. An affirmative determination triggers the sanctions in sections 302 through 316. Section 322 defines a 'war of aggression' to include a ground assault, blockade, drone or missile attack, or physically damaging cyberattack in the 30 days before a determination.

sections.label: Section 302 — Sanctions on Russian Financial Institutions

items.main: Forces sanctions on major Russian banks once the trigger is met.
items.detail: Upon an affirmative determination, the President must within 15 days impose blocking sanctions on three or more of thirteen named institutions — including Sberbank, VTB, Gazprombank, Promsvyazbank, and the Central Bank of the Russian Federation — and must periodically list and sanction additional significant Russian-government-owned financial institutions.

items.main: Sanctions Russia's state nuclear company and its partners, with a medical-isotope waiver.
items.detail: Requires sanctions on Rosatom, its subsidiaries, and foreign persons engaged in significant nuclear-reactor-construction transactions with Rosatom, but lets the President waive them for transactions necessary to produce medical or industrial isotopes if domestic supply is insufficient and the U.S. is taking steps to build non-Rosatom supply chains.

sections.label: Section 314 — Duties on the Russian Federation

items.main: Imposes tariffs of at least 500% on all imports from Russia after a trigger determination.
items.detail: Requires the President, within 15 days of an affirmative determination, to raise the duty on all goods and services imported from Russia to a rate of not less than 500 percent ad valorem, and to report within 60 days on the impact of the tariffs.

sections.label: Section 316 — Taxing Capital Gains on Russian Sovereign Assets

items.main: Taxes income from frozen Russian and Belarusian state assets at 100 percent.
items.detail: Within 15 days of an affirmative determination, imposes a tax equal to 100 percent of the 'disqualified income' (interest or dividends on blocked assets) of the Russian and Belarusian governments, with 100 percent withholding, applied notwithstanding any U.S. treaty obligation. The revenue flows into the Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund.

sections.label: Section 321 — Congressional Review of Russia Sanctions

items.main: Blocks the President from easing Russia sanctions without congressional review.
items.detail: Before terminating, waiving, or significantly altering Russia sanctions (under this Act or a list of named executive orders), the President must report to Congress and observe a 30-day review period during which the action cannot take effect unless a joint resolution of approval is enacted; a joint resolution of disapproval can block the action, with expedited procedures in both chambers.
